content.user_title: Instrument Apps with Azure Application Insights
content.value_statement: Application teams need consistent telemetry setup across languages and Azure hosting services. This skill provides targeted SDK, infrastructure, environment, and query guidance for Application Insights.
actual_capabilities: Explains portal auto-instrumentation for supported Azure App Service applications.
Provides manual SDK setup guidance for ASP.NET Core, Node.js, and Python.
Supplies Bicep and Azure CLI examples for Application Insights and Log Analytics resources.
Covers Container Apps metrics, logs, distributed tracing, Dapr, and KQL diagnostics.
Summarizes Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry options for Python, TypeScript, and Java.
limitations: The skill provides reference guidance and directs project modification requests to azure-prepare.
Azure CLI examples require installed tools, authentication, and suitable resource permissions.
Examples contain placeholders and require validation against the target subscription and hosting environment.
Direct application guidance focuses on ASP.NET Core, Node.js, and Python; Java coverage is limited.

use_cases.title: Plan SDK Instrumentation
use_cases.description: Select the appropriate Application Insights setup and initialization order for a supported application stack.

use_cases.title: Configure Azure Observability
use_cases.description: Plan Application Insights, Log Analytics, environment variables, and infrastructure changes for an Azure workload.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Container Apps
use_cases.description: Use metrics, logs, traces, and KQL guidance to assess Azure Container Apps observability.

prompt_templates.title: Choose an Instrumentation Method
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain whether my [language] application hosted on [service] supports automatic instrumentation. Compare it with manual SDK setup.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Manual Setup Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan Application Insights instrumentation for my [framework] application on [Azure service]. Include package, initialization, configuration, and deployment steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review Azure Infrastructure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Application Insights and Log Analytics design for [workload]. Identify required Bicep or Azure CLI changes and configuration risks.

prompt_templates.title: Design Distributed Observability
prompt_templates.prompt: Design tracing and diagnostics for [services] on Azure Container Apps. Cover correlation, sampling, Dapr, role naming, and useful KQL investigations.

output_examples.input: Should I instrument an ASP.NET Core app hosted on Azure App Service automatically or with the SDK?
output: Check whether the runtime and App Service configuration support portal auto-instrumentation.
Prefer automatic instrumentation when supported and no custom telemetry pipeline is required.
Use the SDK when custom spans, processors, or application-level controls are needed.

output_examples.input: What should I configure for Application Insights in a Node.js service?
output: Install the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry package.
Load configuration before initializing telemetry, then initialize before other instrumented modules.
Provide the connection string through deployment configuration or a managed secret reference.
Deploy and verify requests, dependencies, exceptions, and service role names.

output_examples.input: How can I investigate repeated restarts in Azure Container Apps?
output: Review built-in restart metrics and Container Apps system logs.
Group restart events by application and revision over a relevant time window.
Correlate revision changes with console errors, scaling activity, and trace failures.

best_practices: Confirm the application language, framework, and hosting environment before choosing an instrumentation method.
Keep connection values in managed configuration or secret references, and never commit real values.
Initialize telemetry early, then validate traces, dependencies, logs, sampling, and service identity after deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode connection values in source files or infrastructure examples.
Avoid full production sampling without evaluating traffic volume, cost, and diagnostic requirements.
Do not treat infrastructure metrics as a replacement for application traces and dependency telemetry.

faq.question: Which application stacks are covered?
faq.answer: The main guides cover ASP.NET Core, Node.js, and Python, with shorter TypeScript, Python exporter, Java, and Container Apps references.

faq.question: When should I use automatic instrumentation?
faq.answer: Use it for supported Azure App Service runtimes when standard telemetry is sufficient and application code changes are unnecessary.

faq.question: Can this skill modify my application?
faq.answer: It primarily provides guidance and reference material. Its instructions direct component addition and project modification requests to azure-prepare.

faq.question: How should I store the Application Insights connection string?
faq.answer: Use deployment environment configuration or a managed secret reference. Do not place real values in source control.

faq.question: Does it cover Azure Container Apps?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Log Analytics, built-in metrics, SDK setup, distributed tracing, Dapr, and diagnostic KQL queries.

faq.question: What access is needed for the Azure CLI examples?
faq.answer: You need Azure CLI authentication and permissions to read, create, or update the referenced Azure resources.
